text:
alex: heads-up — seeing a big latency spike on eu-west apiserver fleet, proxy connection pools are nearly saturated and a bunch of GPU pod creates are failing with 503s to the apiserver. Scheduler is timing out on bind calls.

maria: ugh, any recent changes rolled there?

alex: pushed a metrics rollout 30m ago (kube-metrics 1.4.2) and a small kube-proxy tweak. not obvious but dashboards show apiserver CPU at ~95% on 2 nodes and request queues growing. controller-manager shows repeated 429s.

sam: link to graphs?

alex: https://grafana.redwood.svc/d/CP/eu-west-controlplane?orgId=1

alex: snippet from apiserver logs:
```
I0318 10:12:41.123456 1 wrap.go:47] PUT /api/v1/namespaces/ai/pods: (45.672ms) 503
E0318 10:12:41.123789 1 dispatcher.go:112] watch cache failed: too many events, dropping connection
E0318 10:12:41.124001 1 authentication.go:123] token validation failed: etcdclient: leader transfer in progress
```

toni: that watch cache error + leader transfer message feels like etcd pressure too. any spikes on etcd disk iops or followers?

alex: etcd leader election churned once around the same time, iops look elevated on the leader host (+30% write latency). logs show compact spikes.

indra: controller-manager 429s mean kube-controller is being throttled — that would explain scheduling delays for GPU allocations. we should reduce control-plane request volume first. can we temporarily scale down the metrics deployment?

maria: if we scale down metrics, we risk losing observability data. but short-term relief makes sense. do we have an alternative region to route control traffic to for scheduled jobs?

sam: routing control-plane traffic cross-region is messy for apiserver certs and latency. quicker: bump apiserver replicas in eu-west from 3 -> 5 and increase --max-requests-inflight and --max-mutating-requests-inflight for now. also consider reducing watch cache size TTL.

alex: action plan: 1) create incident, 2) scale down kube-metrics from 6 -> 1, 3) scale apiserver replicas 3->5 and set --max-requests-inflight=200/ --max-mutating-requests-inflight=50, 4) if no improvement, failover some non-critical namespaces to eu-central. doing 1-3 now.

sre-bot: Incident INC-2026-0443 opened by alex — Priority P1 — "eu-west apiserver proxy saturation / GPU scheduling 503s"

toni: i'll watch etcd leader and iops metrics, and pre-stage a snapshot in case we need to restore.

alex: scaled metrics down, new apiserver replicas created and started. applied flags via rollout.

indra: controller-manager 429s dropped immediately, scheduler bind latency improving.

maria: apiserver p95 latency back to normal levels — monitors green. need a postmortem and runbook changes so metrics releases don't overwhelm control plane.

sam: followups: 1) add QoS cap on metrics to limit burst QPS to apiserver, 2) add autoscale policy for apiserver control-plane nodes, 3) investigate etcd compaction timing and disk provisioning for leader host.

alex: filing followups in INC-2026-0443. great job everyone :thumbsup:
